attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense claim. The normalised wording keeps the core point: no real buyers outside the labs that hyperscalers subsidise. The surrounding text also counts hyperscalers among those who can pay, and the contract accounts for this.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. It treats 'built for no-one' as hyperbole, excludes hyperscalers and their labs as counterexamples, and allows for the speaker's 'few billion' of outside demand. Testing concentration and exclusivity separately matches the two clauses of the sentence.

evidence.note: Dated 2026-04-15, inside the period. Jane Street is a profitable trading firm, neither a hyperscaler nor a subsidised lab, and it committed $6B to AI cloud compute. One outside buyer at that size goes beyond the speaker's 'few billion' allowance for all outside demand.

The Information, via The Decoder, reports that OpenAI and Anthropic hold roughly half of about $2T in big-cloud backlog. This supports heavy concentration, but half is not 'overwhelming', and the base includes non-AI contracts.

reviews.rationale: The concentration part holds: the two loss-making labs account for about half of the big clouds' backlog. The exclusivity part fails: Jane Street, a profitable non-lab buyer, committed $6B to AI compute in April 2026. That one deal exceeds the speaker's 'few billion' allowance and meets the contract's contradiction condition. Since the contract tests the two parts separately, the result is mixed.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his figure.

semantics.note: Both the 50%-or-more share and the roughly $748B total are kept. This is a firm present-tense statement of fact.

contract.note: Limiting 'hyperscalers' to Microsoft, Google and AWS fits the speaker's own $748B figure. Reading 'now' as the March 2026 quarter plus later deals is reasonable but affects the result, as do headline deal values versus booked RPO.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure: commercial RPO of $627B at 2026-03-31. This is part of the base, and the OpenAI share at this date is not given.
Microsoft's figure that 45% of RPO was tied to OpenAI dates from 2025-12-31, before the target period.
Press estimate, unconfirmed by either company, that Anthropic's Google commitment is about $200B, over 40% of a backlog above $460B. It covers one piece of the numerator.
The 'roughly half' estimate uses a base that includes Oracle, about $2T, which is a different company set from the contract's three. It also gives AWS's $364B backlog.
Secondary summary citing Alphabet's 10-Q: Google Cloud backlog of $462B at the end of Q1 2026. This is part of the base.

reviews.rationale: The three-company base is about $1.45T, so half is about $727B. Only Microsoft disclosed a lab share, and that figure predates the period. Google and Amazon disclose none. The lab deals in the packet put the share somewhere near 45-50%, depending on deal timing and whether headline values are booked. The only outside estimate of 'roughly half' includes Oracle. The evidence neither clearly passes nor clearly fails the 50% / about $748B test.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps both parts, the 'appears' hedge, and the Claude uptime carve-out. It is a hedged impression posed alongside a rhetorical question.

contract.note: The speaker sets no measure, and 'appears' hedges both parts. Any test, such as treating usage limits as a failure to serve customers, would be the evaluator's own reading. Leaving it unscored is fair.

evidence.note: Anthropic cut peak-hour limits to match demand to capacity in March 2026. That would matter for a firm version of the claim, but the claim is hedged and not scored.

reviews.rationale: Both parts are hedged with 'appears' and set no measurable threshold for being unable to serve customers or for compute-driven product improvement. Scoring would require a test the speaker never supplied. Evidence such as Anthropic's peak-hour limits is context only.
